name: Width by processing left and right differently (L/R EQ, one-sided saturation, formant shift, slap times) with a mono-safe parallel blend
goal: Widen synths, pads and FX by making the left and right channels genuinely different - double-tracked or alternate sources hard-panned, different L/R EQ, saturation on only one side, a formant-shifted duplicate on one side, and a short slap delay at different times per side (about 50 vs 75 ms) - and blend any phase-risky width (Haas/width plus distortion) in parallel beside an untouched dry chain so mono compatibility is preserved; delta beyond the existing Haas, mid/side and unison skills.

source.title: 12 Ways To Widen Your Sounds Like A Pro

prerequisites: DAW/Web Audio graph with per-channel (L/R) EQ, saturation, delay and a parallel rack/splitter

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Mono-ish synth, lead, pad, clap or FX layer to widen

outputs.name: widened_layer
outputs.description: Wider layer that still survives mono summing

steps.action: Most organic: make L and R different sources - record an analog synth part twice, or use two different claps/variants - and hard-pan one left and one right.
steps.expect: Wide image with no phase issues

steps.action: L/R EQ: EQ each side differently (e.g. brighter left; right with highs reduced and mids boosted).
Mid/side EQ only helps if the sound already has side content (a single mono output has none): boost sides more than mid.

Parallel width chain: keep a dry chain untouched and add a second chain with a Haas/width effect followed by distortion; mix the wet chain in slowly until width appears while mono compatibility stays good.
steps.expect: Width added without removing the mono centre

steps.action: Saturate only one side (pan the drive to the right, leaving the left clean).
Chorus as the old-school widener for mono synths - note it can sterilise the tone.

Haas via delay (widest but sacrifices phase integrity): one side ~1 ms, the other ~6-20 ms, low feedback, EQ the delay; reserve it for supplemental pads/layers and avoid stacking it on already-reverbed/delayed sounds.
steps.expect: Very wide but less mono-safe; use sparingly

steps.action: Formant-shift one duplicate and leave the other unshifted, panned apart.
Slap delay return: about 50 ms on one side and 75 ms on the other (tape-style delay preferred), feedback to taste - cleaner and less unnatural than Haas.

Synth-side: two otherwise identical saws with a different waveform variant on one, panned L/R with the random(-phase) control turned down; or unison with per-voice pan and fine detune; or pan different filters per side; reverb also adds width.
Check the mono sum after each method and back off the risky ones first.
steps.expect: No large level/tone collapse in mono

verification: Mono sum of the final layer keeps its body (no obvious cancellation)
Parallel width chain at 0% equals the dry sound
L/R difference is audible when soloing each channel
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth/DAW vendors named in the source video.
Delta only: Haas basics live in haas-plus-phase-offset-width-automated, mid/side EQ in midside-eq-bass-focus-width-depth, unison width in unison-odd-even-detune-width-clean-supersaw.
Web Audio mapping: ChannelSplitterNode -> per-channel BiquadFilter/WaveShaper/DelayNode -> ChannelMergerNode, with a dry/wet GainNode pair for the parallel blend.
